newsitem.title: GERMANY: FIGURE SKATING-ELDREDGE INCLUDED IN CHAMPIONS SERIES FINAL.
newsitem.headline: FIGURE SKATING-ELDREDGE INCLUDED IN CHAMPIONS SERIES FINAL.

text.p: World figure skating champion Todd Eldredge was included on Monday in the six-man field for the Champions Series final in Canada next year despite dropping out of the second of his two official scoring events of the series last month.

The management committee of the Champions Series decided that Eldredge's points from the Lalique Trophy in Paris last month, a non-scoring event for the American, could be substituted for his designated second event, the NHK Trophy in Osaka last month, where he pulled out with an ankle injury just before he was to skate.

Under Series rules, skaters had to nominate two scoring events from the six competitions making up the series, plus a third, non-scoring event where points could be collected for use should a competitor be prevented from taking part in a designated tournament.

The six-event Champions Series ended in St Petersburg on Sunday. The leading six men and women, five dance couples and four pairs qualify for the series finals in Hamilton, Ontario, from February 28 to March 2.

Eldredge won Skate America to open the series and his 12 points from the Lalique Trophy put him joint first in the men's standings with former world champion Elvis Stojko of Canada and Russian Olympic champion Alexei Urmanov, who also won two events each.
They each had 24 points. The three others in the men's final will be Russians Ilya Kulik (18 points) and Alexei Yagudin (16), along with Dmitry Dmitrenko of Ukraine (16).

American world champion Michelle Kwan and European champion Irina Slutskaya of Russia head the women's standings with 24 points. Joining them in the final will be Russian Maria Butyrskaya (21 points), Americans Tonia Kwiatkowski (18) and Tara Lipinski (16), and Russian Olga Markova (14).

The five dance couples for Hamilton will be Russians Anjelika Krylova and Oleg Ovsiannikov (24 points), Marina Anissina and Gwendal Peizerat of France (21), Canadians Shae-Lynn Bourne and Victor Kraatz (21), Sophie Moniotte and Pascal Lavanchy of France (19) and Russians Irina Lobacheva and Ilia Averbukh (18).

The pairs field will comprise Germans Mandy Woetzel and Ingo Steuer (24 points), Americans Jenni Meno and Todd Sand (21), and two Russian couples, Oksana Kazakova and Artur Dmitriev (19) and world champions Marina Eltsova and Andrei Bushkov (18).
